comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM disclose the recognition of compensation expense over a vesting period for unvested employee awards. GS specifically links this to 'overrides related to investment management services' with an expense of $376 million in 2024. JPM discloses a similar mechanism for 'employee share-based incentive plans,' noting $963 million (pretax) of unamortized compensation expense for unvested awards expected to be amortized over 1.6 years, but does not specify the dollar amount of expense recognized for the year in this specific excerpt, nor does it mention overrides. Both confirm the non-capitalization of these costs.

sentences.text: The firm shares a portion of its overrides related to investment management services with approximately 900 employees, including with the firm's executive officers.
The fair value of these overrides is recognized as compensation expense over the vesting period.
Such expense was $376 million for 2024, $407 million for 2023 and $493 million for 2022.
The Firm recognized the following noncash compensation expense related to its various employee share-based incentive plans in its Consolidated statements of income.
At December 31, 2024, approximately $963 million (pretax) of compensation expense related to unvested awards had not yet been charged to net income.
That cost is expected to be amortized into compensation expense over a weighted-average period of 1.6 years.
The Firm does not capitalize any compensation expense related to share-based compensation awards to employees.

comparisons.peer_topic: DCP Compensation Expense Calculation and Recognition
comparisons.peer_summary: Compensation expense for Deferred Cash-Based Compensation (DCP) awards is based on the notional value adjusted for changes in the fair value of employee-selected referenced investments, and is recognized over the vesting period of each separately vesting portion.
comparisons.comparison: MS and GS both disclose compensation expense recognition for deferred equity-like awards over the vesting period, linked to fair value changes. GS recognizes expense for 'overrides related to investment management services' shared with ~900 employees, totaling $376 million in 2024. MS recognizes expense for 'Deferred Cash-Based Compensation (DCP) awards' based on notional value adjusted for fair value changes of referenced investments. Both explicitly state that expense is recognized over the vesting period.

sentences.text: The firm shares a portion of its overrides related to investment management services with approximately 900 employees, including with the firm's executive officers.
The fair value of these overrides is recognized as compensation expense over the vesting period.
Such expense was $376 million for 2024, $407 million for 2023 and $493 million for 2022.
Compensation expense for DCP awards is calculated based on the notional value of the award granted, adjusted for changes in the fair value of the referenced investments that employees select.
Compensation expense is recognized over the vesting period relevant to each separately vesting portion of deferred awards.
